lines: Revolut founder and CEO Nik Storonsky describes scaling to about 80 million customers by treating products as disciplined, data-validated bets, growing organically with cheaper, better alternatives to legacy services such as multi-currency cards and business accounts rather than early paid marketing.

Under its 'new bets' process, small autonomous teams launch products that are measured against historical revenue and retention cohorts; laggards are shut down and winners scaled through an automated, LLM-assisted cross-sell engine that acts like a virtual account manager.
He favors subscription and transaction revenue over interest-heavy lending to reduce credit-cycle risk and support a higher valuation multiple.

For the US, Revolut plans a credit-card-led push against premium incumbents like Amex and Chase; Storonsky says good markets have 'sleepy' incumbents and favorable interchange and credit rules, and that winning users under 35 is the path to primary-bank status.
He backs quarterly rather than annual performance reviews to exit underperformers faster, and says AI is shifting teams toward generalists and shrinking the headcount needed to launch products.
title: Nik Storonsky: The most uncompromising banking CEO
